# Changes

1. Moment functions now locate Y, A, W, Z, X by column name. Previously they used
   global position indices (col.Y = 1, col.A = 2, ...) set in the synthetic-data
   section, and proximal_bridge() only re-assigned these locally, which does not
   affect functions defined in the global environment. The chamber data frame has
   columns (U, Y, A, W, Z, X, Y1, Y0), so the bridge functions were run with U as Y,
   Y as A, A as W, W as Z and Z as X. That is where the broken bridge estimates in
   the previous knitted pdf came from (42.8, 80.3, 591.8, 1709.4).
2. Proximal() now fits the ivreg used for starting values on the data it is given.
   It previously used whatever IVReg object was left in the workspace, which was the
   fit on the synthetic example.
3. The bootstrap loop resampled Data (the synthetic example) instead of the chamber
   data. It now resamples the data it is given.
4. `data_weak_conf$df` and `data_strong_conf$df` did not exist (the objects are
   called `..._linear` / `..._non_linear`), so the file did not knit as-is.
5. Z, W, X are standardised and Y is min-max normalised before fitting, with Y1 and
   Y0 normalised using the same constants so the true ATE is on the same scale as
   the estimates. This keeps exp() in the q bridge from overflowing. The q fit is
   tried from two starting points and the moment value at the optimum is reported,
   so a failed fit is visible.
6. Added raw measurement scales for A and Y per benchmark, and
   diagnostics for confounding strength and proxy informativeness.

```{r}
library(ivreg)
set.seed(2026)
```

# Estimators (following presentation slides)

All functions expect a data frame with named columns Y, A, W, Z, X, with A binary
in {0,1}. Roles in the proximal DAG:

* Y outcome, A treatment, X observed baseline covariate
* Z treatment-inducing confounding proxy (associated with U and A, no direct effect on Y)
* W outcome-inducing confounding proxy (associated with U and Y, not caused by A or Z)

## Outcome bridge h (linear)

h(a, w, x) = b_a + b_w w + b_x x, one parameter vector per treatment arm, solving
E[ 1{A=a} g(Z,X) {Y - h(a,W,X)} ] = 0 with g(Z,X) = (1, Z, X).

```{r}
h.linear <- function(data, theta) {
  as.vector(cbind(1, data$W, data$X) %*% theta)
}

moment.h <- function(data, theta, a) {
  ind <- if (a == 1) data$A else 1 - data$A
  Residuals <- ind * cbind(1, data$Z, data$X) *
    (data$Y - h.linear(data, theta))
  sum(colMeans(Residuals)^2)
}
```

## Treatment bridge q (log-linear)

q(a, z, x) = exp(c_a + c_z z + c_x x), playing the role of an inverse probability
weight, solving E[ {1 - 1{A=a} q(a,Z,X)} g(W,X) ] = 0 with g(W,X) = (1, W, X).

```{r}
q.exp <- function(data, theta) {
  exp(as.vector(cbind(1, data$Z, data$X) %*% theta))
}

moment.q <- function(data, theta, a) {
  ind <- if (a == 1) data$A else 1 - data$A
  Residuals <- as.vector(1 - ind * q.exp(data, theta)) * cbind(1, data$W, data$X)
  sum(colMeans(Residuals)^2)
}
```

## Proximal estimators: OR, IPW, AIPW

```{r}
Proximal <- function(data, maxit = 5000) {
  ## starting values for h from the 2SLS fit on this data
  IVReg <- ivreg::ivreg(Y ~ A + W + X | A + Z + X, data = data)
  b <- IVReg$coefficients   # (Intercept), A, W, X

  ctrl <- list(maxit = maxit)
  h1.opt <- optim(par = c(b[1] + b[2], b[3], b[4]),
                  fn = function(th) moment.h(data, th, 1), control = ctrl)
  h0.opt <- optim(par = c(b[1], b[3], b[4]),
                  fn = function(th) moment.h(data, th, 0), control = ctrl)

  ## starting values for q from a propensity glm, tried with both signs
  g <- suppressWarnings(
    glm(A ~ Z + X, data = data, family = "binomial")$coefficients)
  best.q <- function(a) {
    fits <- lapply(list(g, -g), function(init)
      optim(par = init, fn = function(th) moment.q(data, th, a), control = ctrl))
    fits[[which.min(sapply(fits, `[[`, "value"))]]
  }
  q1.opt <- best.q(1)
  q0.opt <- best.q(0)

  h1.hat <- h.linear(data, h1.opt$par)
  h0.hat <- h.linear(data, h0.opt$par)
  q1.hat <- q.exp(data, q1.opt$par)
  q0.hat <- q.exp(data, q0.opt$par)

  ATE.OR   <- mean(h1.hat - h0.hat)
  ATE.IPW  <- mean(data$A * q1.hat * data$Y - (1 - data$A) * q0.hat * data$Y)
  ATE.AIPW <- mean(data$A * q1.hat * (data$Y - h1.hat) -
                   (1 - data$A) * q0.hat * (data$Y - h0.hat) +
                   (h1.hat - h0.hat))

  list(est = c(OR = ATE.OR, IPW = ATE.IPW, AIPW = ATE.AIPW),
       moments = c(h1 = h1.opt$value, h0 = h0.opt$value,
                   q1 = q1.opt$value, q0 = q0.opt$value))
}

ProximalBoot <- function(data, B = 100) {
  est <- t(replicate(B, Proximal(data[sample(nrow(data), replace = TRUE), ])$est))
  apply(est, 2, quantile, c(0.025, 0.975))
}
```

## Reference estimators

```{r}
naive_regression <- function(data) coef(lm(Y ~ A, data = data))["A"]
backdoor_adjustment <- function(data) coef(lm(Y ~ A + X + Z + W, data = data))["A"]
oracle_U_adjustment <- function(data) coef(lm(Y ~ A + X + Z + W + U, data = data))["A"]
proximal_IVReg <- function(data)
  coef(ivreg::ivreg(Y ~ A + W + X | A + Z + X, data = data))["A"]
```

# Check on the synthetic example from the slides

True ATE = 1 by construction. OLS with or without the proxies as covariates is
biased, proximal 2SLS and the bridge estimators should be approximately unbiased.

```{r}
expit <- function(v) exp(v) / (1 + exp(v))
set.seed(123)
N <- 1000
X <- rnorm(N); U <- rnorm(N)
Z <- 0.2 * U + X + rnorm(N) * 0.25
W <- 0.2 * U + X + rnorm(N) * 0.25
A <- rbinom(N, 1, expit(0.2 + 0.25 * Z + 0.1 * X + 0.25 * U))
Y0 <- 2 * U + W + X + rnorm(N) * 0.25
Y1 <- 1 + 2 * U + W + X + rnorm(N) * 0.25
Y <- A * Y1 + (1 - A) * Y0
SynthData <- data.frame(Y = Y, A = A, W = W, Z = Z, X = X, U = U)

c(true.ATE       = mean(Y1 - Y0),
  naive          = naive_regression(SynthData),
  adjust.X       = coef(lm(Y ~ A + X, data = SynthData))["A"],
  backdoor.XZW   = backdoor_adjustment(SynthData),
  proximal.2SLS  = proximal_IVReg(SynthData))
```

```{r}
synth.prox <- Proximal(SynthData)
synth.prox$est
synth.prox$moments  # moment values at the optimum, should be near 0
```

# Causal Chambers benchmarks

Variable roles in the light tunnel (appendix E of the paper): U = green (hidden
light source, drive 0-255), Y = ir_3, A = led_3_uv (binary, drive 0 or 2047),
W = pol_1, Z = led_2_uv, X = red.

Preprocessing: Y min-max normalised to [0,1], Y1/Y0 normalised with the same
constants so the true ATE is on the estimation scale, A mapped from {0,2047} to
{0,1}, W, Z, X, U standardised (mean 0, sd 1).

```{r}
normalize_with <- function(x, lo, hi) (x - lo) / (hi - lo)

load_cc_data <- function(path) {
  raw <- read.csv(path)
  stopifnot(all(raw$led_3_uv %in% c(0, 2047)))
  ylo <- min(raw$ir_3); yhi <- max(raw$ir_3)
  df <- data.frame(
    U  = as.numeric(scale(raw$green)),
    Y  = normalize_with(raw$ir_3, ylo, yhi),
    A  = raw$led_3_uv / 2047,
    W  = as.numeric(scale(raw$pol_1)),
    Z  = as.numeric(scale(raw$led_2_uv)),
    X  = as.numeric(scale(raw$red)),
    Y1 = normalize_with(raw$Y1, ylo, yhi),
    Y0 = normalize_with(raw$Y0, ylo, yhi))
  raw_scales <- c(
    n         = nrow(raw),
    P.A1      = mean(raw$led_3_uv > 0),
    Y.mean    = mean(raw$ir_3), Y.sd = sd(raw$ir_3),
    Y.min     = ylo,            Y.max = yhi,
    ATE.raw   = mean(raw$Y1 - raw$Y0))
  list(df = df, raw = raw_scales)
}

bench.files <- c(
  `1 weak linear`       = "N6000_out_binaryA_counterfactuals_weak_confounding_linear.csv",
  `2 weak non-linear`   = "N6000_out_binaryA_counterfactuals_weak_confounding_non_linear.csv",
  `3 strong linear`     = "N6000_out_binaryA_counterfactuals_strong_confounding_linear.csv",
  `4 strong non-linear` = "N6000_out_binaryA_counterfactuals_strong_confounding_non_linear.csv")

benchmarks <- lapply(bench.files, load_cc_data)
```

## Raw measurement scales

Y (ir_3) is a sensor reading in raw counts and A switches led_3_uv between drive
levels 0 and 2047. The raw ATE is about 3500 counts in all four benchmarks, i.e.
the treatment adds the same amount of infrared light in every setting. The
normalised true ATEs differ across benchmarks mainly because the range of Y (the
normalisation denominator) is wider under strong confounding, where the light
source also reaches sensor 3. Normalising by a fixed constant instead of the
per-dataset range would make ATEs comparable across benchmarks.

```{r}
round(t(sapply(benchmarks, `[[`, "raw")), 2)
```

## True ATEs (normalised)

```{r}
true.ATE <- sapply(benchmarks, function(b) mean(b$df$Y1 - b$df$Y0))
round(true.ATE, 4)
```

## All estimators on all benchmarks

```{r}
run_all <- function(b) {
  prox <- Proximal(b$df)
  c(true.ATE      = mean(b$df$Y1 - b$df$Y0),
    naive         = unname(naive_regression(b$df)),
    backdoor.XZW  = unname(backdoor_adjustment(b$df)),
    oracle.XZWU   = unname(oracle_U_adjustment(b$df)),
    proximal.2SLS = unname(proximal_IVReg(b$df)),
    prox.OR       = unname(prox$est["OR"]),
    prox.IPW      = unname(prox$est["IPW"]),
    prox.AIPW     = unname(prox$est["AIPW"]))
}
results <- sapply(benchmarks, run_all)
round(results, 4)
```

Moment values at the optimum for the bridge fits. These should be near 0, large
values mean the fit failed or the parametric form does not hold:

```{r}
round(t(sapply(benchmarks, function(b) Proximal(b$df)$moments)), 6)
```

## Bootstrap 95% intervals for the bridge estimators

```{r}
set.seed(2026)
boot.CIs <- lapply(benchmarks, function(b) round(ProximalBoot(b$df, B = 100), 4))
boot.CIs
```

# Diagnostics: confounding strength and proxy informativeness

The chamber records the counterfactuals, so confounding can be measured directly
as the association between Y(0) and A (the association of
Y_a and A given all variables not caused by A). Under no confounding, Y(0) is
independent of A.

```{r}
confounding_diag <- function(df) {
  c(`E[Y0|A=1]-E[Y0|A=0]` = mean(df$Y0[df$A == 1]) - mean(df$Y0[df$A == 0]),
    `Y0~A | Z,W,X`        = coef(lm(Y0 ~ A + Z + W + X, data = df))["A"],
    `Y0~A | Z,W,X,U`      = coef(lm(Y0 ~ A + Z + W + X + U, data = df))["A"],
    `R2: U ~ Z+W+X`       = summary(lm(U ~ Z + W + X, data = df))$r.squared)
}
round(t(sapply(benchmarks, function(b) confounding_diag(b$df))), 4)
```

Reading the table: column 1 is the raw difference in Y(0) between treated and
control, column 2 is what remains after linear adjustment for the proxies,
column 3 additionally adjusts for U, column 4 is the R squared of U regressed on
(Z, W, X). If column 2 is close to 0, conditioning on the proxies already removes
most of the confounding and backdoor adjustment is expected to do well. This is
This shows whether the proxies carry enough signal to reconstruct U.

# Summary

Errors relative to the true ATE:

```{r}
err <- sweep(results[-1, , drop = FALSE], 2, results["true.ATE", ], "-")
round(err, 4)
```

Absolute error ranking per benchmark (smaller is better):

```{r}
apply(abs(err), 2, function(v) names(sort(v)))
```
